summary: Full backend + frontend test of the new Live Classes module. Backend: 25 pytest cases (admin CRUD, RBAC, grade-range scoping, curriculum scoping, draft/publish, sorting, parent union) all PASS; 6 additional edge cases documented as xfail validation gaps. Frontend: admin /admin/live-classes create/edit/delete flow, child /calendar upcoming-live-past split with join/recording links and hidden-class scoping, parent header link + parent calendar, and mobile layout all PASS. All test data was deleted; DB live_classes collection back to 0 docs, no user/school mutations made.

critical.issue: Unhandled ValueError -> HTTP 500 when min_grade/max_grade/duration_minutes are non-numeric (e.g. min_grade='abc', duration_minutes='xyz'). int() is called on raw body outside any try/validation. Should return 400.

minor.issue: scheduled_at is stored verbatim with no ISO-8601 validation; 'not-a-date' is accepted (200). The stored string is also used for the Mongo sort, so mixed/invalid formats break ordering, and the UI then renders 'Invalid Date' and buckets the class into Past Classes.
Whitespace-only title ('   ') accepted; title is not trimmed before the required-field check.
No range validation: min_grade > max_grade accepted (creates a class invisible to every user), grades outside 0-5 accepted, negative duration_minutes (-30) accepted.

meeting_link / recording_url scheme not validated - 'javascript:alert(1)' is stored and rendered directly into an <a href> shown to children/parents (admin-only input, so low exploitability, but should be restricted to http/https).
No pydantic response model; endpoint relies on to_list(1000) with no pagination. Fine at current scale, worth noting.

issues: Past classes are sorted oldest-first (16 Aug listed above 17 Aug) because the backend sorts scheduled_at ascending for both buckets. Past/recording lists read better most-recent-first.
Future (non-live) class CTA is labelled 'Join Link' which is awkward wording for K-5 users; 'Join' or 'Open Join Link' would be clearer.
'Live Classes' link is white text on the light-green header pill - contrast is on the low side (matches existing sibling links, so pre-existing pattern, cosmetic only).

action_items: Wrap int() coercions in POST/PUT /api/admin/live-classes (min_grade, max_grade, duration_minutes) with validation and return 400 instead of 500 - ideally move the whole body to a Pydantic model.
Validate scheduled_at as ISO-8601 on create/update (and normalise to UTC) so sorting and UI date rendering cannot break.
Trim title and reject whitespace-only; validate min_grade <= max_grade, grades within 0-5, duration_minutes > 0.
Restrict meeting_link / recording_url to http(s) URLs before storing.
OPTIONAL UX: render Past Classes newest-first on /calendar.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/live_classes.py create/update: `int(body.get(...))` on unvalidated request JSON is the only 500 in the module - use a Pydantic request model (LiveClassCreate/LiveClassUpdate) to get 422/400 for free and to document the contract.
scheduled_at is both the sort key and a raw client string - a single malformed value corrupts ordering for all users; parse with datetime.fromisoformat and store a canonical UTC ISO string.

GET /live-classes falls through to the child branch for any non-parent authed role (teacher/school admin) using user['grade'] which teachers do not have -> they get grade 0 scoping silently. Consider an explicit role check or an admin/teacher-specific view.
Frontend LiveClassesPage.fetchClasses only console.errors on failure - there is no visible error state; a failed GET is indistinguishable from 'no classes scheduled yet'.

success_rate.backend: 100% (25/25 functional; 6 known validation gaps recorded as xfail)

rca_of_the_issue: The 500s come from routes/live_classes.py calling int() directly on unvalidated request-body values (create: min_grade/max_grade/duration_minutes; update: same three fields). A non-numeric string raises ValueError before any HTTPException can be produced, so FastAPI returns 500 (confirmed in backend.err.log: "ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'xyz'"). The other findings are the same root cause class: the endpoint accepts a free-form dict instead of a Pydantic model, so title, scheduled_at, grade range, duration and URL fields are all unvalidated.
